patches.new:
We need one integral over $[0,\pi]$, for integers $j\ge0$ and $l\ge1$:
\[
\int_0^\pi\cos j\theta\cos l\theta\,\dd\theta=\frac\pi2\,\delta_{jl}.
\]
To see it, product-to-sum turns the integrand into $\tfrac12[\cos(j-l)\theta+\cos(j+l)\theta]$. A cosine $\cos k\theta$ with a nonzero integer $k$ integrates over $[0,\pi]$ to $\sin(k\pi)/k=0$. Since $j+l\ge1$, the second term always gives zero; the first gives zero unless $j=l$, in which case it gives $\tfrac12\pi$. If $j=0$ the result is $0$, because $l\ge1$ means $j\ne l$. Now compute, with $\dd u=(2L/\pi)\dd\theta$ and $\cos(n-m)\theta=\cos(|n-m|\theta)$:
\begin{align*}
\bra{n}\cos\tfrac{q\pi x}{L}\ket{m}
&=\int_0^{2L}\frac{1}{2L}\bigl[\cos(|n-m|\theta)-\cos((n+m)\theta)\bigr](-1)^q\cos(2q\theta)\,\dd u\\
&=\frac{(-1)^q}{2L}\cdot\frac{2L}{\pi}\left[\int_0^\pi\cos(|n-m|\theta)\cos(2q\theta)\,\dd\theta-\int_0^\pi\cos((n+m)\theta)\cos(2q\theta)\,\dd\theta\right]\\
&=\frac{(-1)^q}{\pi}\left[\frac\pi2\,\delta_{|n-m|,2q}-\frac\pi2\,\delta_{n+m,2q}\right].
\end{align*}
In the last line we used the integral above with $l=2q\ge2$, and $j=|n-m|$ in the first term (this includes the diagonal case $n=m$, $j=0$, which gives $0$) and $j=n+m$ in the second. Hence

import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
L,Nb=1.0,60
n=np.arange(1,Nb+1); E0=(n*np.pi/(2*L))**2
D=np.abs(n[:,None]-n[None,:]); S=n[:,None]+n[None,:]
C1=-0.5*((D==2)*1.0-(S==2)*1.0)
def ground(c):
    w,v=np.linalg.eigh(np.diag(E0)+c*C1); return w[0],v[:,0]@C1@v[:,0]
cs=np.linspace(0,1.4,200); Es=[ground(c)[0] for c in cs]
